To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mineral levels in rotifers can be effectively increased to levels higher than those found in natural copepod prey by using organic minerals in a short time frame.

the levels of Se, Zn, Mn and Cu found in rotifers (B. plicatilis), can be increased up to and above the known requirements of marine fish larvae, by using organic mineral sources, and that these levels can be retained during rotifer storage.

rotifers can be enriched with the trace elements Mn, Zn, Cu, and Se, to levels higher than those found in copepods, using organic bound minerals, while increasing iodine in rotifer is ineffective at the levels tested.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an enrichment strategy to produce rotifers with high levels of Mn, Zn, Se, Cu and iodine.

increasing the concentration of the essential trace minerals Se, Zn, Mn and Cu in rotifers, which can then be used as a first feeding diet for marine fish larvae, and is the first study to simultaneously increase these minerals in rotifers.
the production of rotifers with high levels of essential trace elements, in order to provide a more complete diet for rearing larval fish.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mineral requirements of fish larvae can be met by using mineral enriched rotifers.

the levels of Mn and Cu in rotifers can be increased up to and beyond the requirements of marine fish larvae, but the levels of Zn and Se in rotifers can only be increased to the levels of copepods, which are higher than those of marine fish larvae.
it is possible to enrich rotifers to copepod levels of Se, Zn, Mn and Cu, but the enrichment of rotifers for iodine was not successful.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
rotifers can be produced with mineral levels higher than fish larval requirements using organic mineral sources.
the use of organically bound minerals in rotifers as live feed is feasible and may be an important tool in the future for the production of high quality live feed.

rotifers enriched with organic mineral sources can be used as a live feed to meet the mineral requirements of marine fish larvae, and that the levels of these essential elements can be increased without affecting larval fish growth.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of organically bound mineral sources is a simple, cost effective and practical method of producing rotifers with elevated mineral levels, which may be beneficial for the rearing of marine larvae.
the use of organic minerals in rotifer diets is an effective way to increase the levels of essential trace elements in rotifers.
rotifers can be enriched with Mn, Cu and Zn to levels higher than those found in copepods.
